figures.label: Figure 1
figures.title: Study area and sampling on Mount Kenya
figures.caption: Figure 1. Study area and sampling on Mount Kenya. (a) Mount Kenya in central Kenya, with Kenya shown within Africa in the inset. (b) Surrounding counties (GADM v4.1). (c) Vegetation zones from the VECEA potential natural vegetation map (van Breugel et al., 2015; Lillesø et al., 2024), with the study area outlined by a dashed box. (d) Sampled plots along the elevational gradient. Grey lines mark 100-m contours from the approximately 30-m Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (European Space Agency & Airbus, 2022).

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.title: Morphology of Arabis alpina
figures.caption: Figure 2. Morphology of Arabis alpina. (a) Plant on rocky substrate (Giovanni Fontana). (b) Raceme with white, four-petalled flowers (Jacek Pietruszewski). (c) Developing siliques above the basal rosette (Johannes Hansen). (d) Dehisced siliques with mature brown seeds (karin_schrieber). Photographs are from iNaturalist (https://www.inaturalist.org) and are shown at different scales.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.title: Environmental variation across 27 source plots
figures.caption: Figure 3. Environmental variation across 27 source plots. (a) June 2021 mean temperature, (b) June 2021 total precipitation and (c) standardised soil PC1 by elevation, and (d) soil PC1 loadings. In (a-c), points are plots, lineas are linear fits and shading indicates 95% confidence intervals. In (d), C, N, P and EC denote organic carbon, total nitrogen, extractable phosphorus and electrical conductivity. In the fitted equations, x is elevation in metres.

figures.label: Figure 4
figures.title: Elevational and trait associations in Arabis alpina
figures.caption: Figure 4. Elevational and trait associations in Arabis alpina. (a) Flowering onset and (b) flowering duration in relation to elevation. (c) Final flowering date in relation to flowering onset. (d) Mean individual seed mass (MISM, mg per seed) and (e) total seed number per plant in relation to elevation. (f) Total seed number per plant in relation to MISM. Points represent individual plants, lines show model predictions and shaded bands indicate 95% confidence intervals. Solid and dashed lines indicate P < 0.05 and P ≥ 0.05, respectively, for tests of a slope of zero. Slopes (β) are expressed per 100 m increase in elevation (a, b, d, e), per day of later flowering onset (c) or per mg increase in MISM (f). MISM is natural-log-transformed in (d), and seed-number slopes in (e, f) are on the log-link scale. Flowering dates are expressed as days from 1 June 2021 (day 1). In (c), predictions are based on fixed effects with random intercepts set to zero. The reported P value tests a slope of zero. A slope of one corresponds to constant flowering duration. R2m and R2c denote marginal and conditional R2, respectively.

figures.label: Figure 5
figures.title: Within- and among-plot associations in Arabis alpina
figures.caption: Figure 5. Within- and among-plot associations in Arabis alpina. (a) Change in final flowering date (days) per one-day delay in flowering onset. (b) Change in expected total seed number per plant on the log-link scale per 1 mg increase in mean individual seed mass (MISM, mg per seed). Within-plot coefficients describe associations with deviations from plot means, and among-plot coefficients describe associations with plot means. Points show estimated coefficients (β), and horizontal bars show 95% Wald confidence intervals. Vertical dashed lines mark zero. In (a), a coefficient of one corresponds to unchanged flowering duration, and coefficients below one correspond to shorter duration with later onset. Significance symbols refer to tests against zero (ns, P ≥ 0.05; ***, P < 0.001).

figures.label: Figure 6
figures.title: Associations of germination with source elevation and 100-seed mass in Arabis alpina
figures.caption: Figure 6. Associations of germination with source elevation and 100-seed mass in Arabis alpina. (a) Elevation-only models. (b) Mass-only and elevation-adjusted mass models. Circles, squares and diamonds distinguish the three model sets in that order. Points are coefficients and bars are 95% confidence intervals. Dashed lines mark zero. Coefficients are per 100 m in (a) and per mg of 100-seed mass in (b). Responses are time to first germination (T0; days), time spread (Tg - T0, days), mean germination rate (MGR, day-1) and germination percentage (GP, coefficients in percentage points). Annotations give coefficients (β), marginal R2 (R2m), conditional R2 (R2c) and significance (ns, P ≥ 0.05, and ***, P < 0.001).

figures.label: Figure 7
figures.title: Baseline and projected reproductive traits of Arabis alpina in June 2021 and 2041-2060
figures.caption: Figure 7. Baseline and projected reproductive traits of Arabis alpina in June 2021 and 2041-2060. (a) Flowering onset. (b) Flowering duration. (c) Mean individual seed mass (MISM). (d) Total seed number per plant. Grey open points show baseline means. Brown and yellow filled points show equally weighted ensemble means under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. Open future points show individual climate-model means. Lines connect baseline and future means. Bars span the 2.5th-97.5th percentiles of plant-level predictions. Annotations give absolute changes and, except for onset, percentage changes relative to baseline. Onset uses days because its percentage change depends on the calendar origin. Table 3 and Fig. S6 give bootstrap confidence intervals for mean changes. Seed-number projections use the revised nbinom2 model with all environmental predictors and without random intercepts.

figures.label: Figure S1
figures.title: Vegetation along the Mount Kenya transect
figures.caption: Figure S1. Vegetation along the Mount Kenya transect. (a) Lower montane wet forest. (b) Upper montane forest-bamboo transition with Podocarpus spp., Hagenia abyssinica, Yushania alpina and Lobelia bambuseti. (c) Moorland with tussock grasses, sedges and Lobelia keniensis. (d) Wet Afro-alpine tussock grassland with young Lobelia rosettes. (e) Upper Afro-alpine grassland and wetland with giant rosette plants. (f) Upper Afro-alpine sedges (Carex spp.), grasses (Festuca spp.) and giant groundsels. (g) Transition to nival vegetation among boulders. (h) Sparse nival vegetation and scree. Photographs by Gerald Kenth Kaniaru.

figures.label: Figure S2
figures.title: Field sampling of Arabis alpina
figures.caption: Figure S2. Field sampling of Arabis alpina. (a) The 200-m belt transect followed an established route from 3,000 to 4,800 m. Eighteen elevation bands with two blocks per band and ten plots per block yielded 36 blocks and 360 plots. Triangles show 27 occupied plots in nine blocks at 3,763-4,567 m. (b) Each block contained ten 5 × 5 m plots placed at random coordinate pairs measured from a fixed corner. Plot boundaries were at least 10 m apart and adjacent blocks were separated by at least 20 m. (c) We sampled 581 well-spaced, separately rooted rosettes of varying size. Stolon-connected rosettes could share a genotype. Positions and distances are schematic.

figures.label: Figure S3
figures.title: Distributions of environmental predictors and reproductive traits
figures.caption: Figure S3. Distributions of environmental predictors and reproductive traits. Histograms show densities and black curves show smoothed density estimates. Yellow bars indicate original scales and grey bars indicate natural-log scales. MISM is mean individual seed mass (mg per seed).

figures.label: Figure S4
figures.title: Germination experiment for Arabis alpina
figures.caption: Figure S4. Germination experiment for Arabis alpina. The schematic shows (1) selection of seeds by maternal accession, (2) allocation of 100 seeds to four dishes, (3) the shared temperature and light regime, (4) random placement and repositioning among and within three monitored incubators and (5) daily germination counts and watering to maintain agar moisture.

figures.label: Figure S5
figures.title: Spearman rank correlations between environmental variables and reproductive traits
figures.caption: Figure S5. Spearman rank correlations between environmental variables and reproductive traits. Cells show Spearman’s ρ. Green denotes positive and brown denotes negative correlations. Soil PC1 summarises standardised soil properties. Onset and duration refer to flowering. T0, time spread (Tg – T0), MGR and GP denote germination onset, spread, mean rate and percentage. Only the lower triangle is shown. Blank cells identify untested pairs: germination responses with MISM or total seed number, and 100-seed mass with variables other than the four germination responses. MISM is mean individual seed mass (mg per seed) and equals 100-seed mass divided by 100, giving a rank correlation of one by construction. Asterisks identify Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted P values (*, P < 0.05; **, P < 0.01; ***, P < 0.001). Unmarked values have adjusted P ≥ 0.05.

figures.label: Figure S6
figures.title: Projected changes in Arabis alpina reproductive traits for 2041-2060 relative to June 2021
figures.caption: Figure S6. Projected changes in Arabis alpina reproductive traits for 2041-2060 relative to June 2021. (a) Flowering onset. (b) Flowering duration. (c) Mean individual seed mass (MISM). (d) Total seed number. Brown and yellow indicate SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. Violin widths show the density of mean changes over 1,000 parametric bootstrap replicates. Points are estimated mean changes, weighted equally across three climate models, and bars are 95% percentile bootstrap intervals. Annotations give changes and confidence limits. Vertical dashed lines mark zero. Seed-number estimates use the revised nbinom2 model without random intercepts.
